rules.title: NJ Security Deposit Law
rules.requirement: A landlord may not collect more than one and one-half months' rent as a security deposit, and yearly increases cannot exceed 10% of the current deposit. The deposit must be held in an interest-bearing New Jersey account with interest paid to the tenant, and returned with itemized deductions within 30 days after the tenancy ends.
rules.key_value: 1.5 months' rent cap; yearly increase max 10%; return within 30 days
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties, including mobile homes
rules.exemptions: Owner-occupied two- or three-family dwelling (tenant may opt in 30 days after written request); interest rules do not apply to seasonal rentals of 125 days or less
rules.quoted_span: one and one-half times one month’s rent ( N.J.S.A. 46:8-21.2 ). It can be less.
rules.interaction: State law; the guide mentions no local override.

rules.title: NJ Anti-Eviction Act
rules.requirement: A residential landlord may not evict or fail to renew a lease without good cause, which must be proven in court. Causes are listed in the Act (nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations, owner occupancy, conversion, and others), generally with a written Notice to Quit or Cease.
rules.key_value: Good cause required; statutory grounds, Notice to Quit (3 days to 3 months by cause)
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential rental properties including single-family homes, mobile homes, apartment buildings, rooming and boarding houses
rules.exemptions: Two- or three-unit owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units (limited grounds still apply); hotel, motel and guest house transient or seasonal guests; unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member
rules.quoted_span: The Anti-Eviction Act,  N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1 to 61.12, was created to protect
rules.interaction: State law applies statewide; the guide does not describe local overrides.

all.unavailable: owner-occupied premises with two or fewer rental units

any.unavailable: hotel, motel or guest house rented to a transient guest or seasonal tenant, or unit held in trust for a developmentally disabled family member

rules.title: NJ Law Against Discrimination: source of lawful income
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent or discriminate in renting because of a person's source of lawful income, among other protected traits. A landlord may still refuse for insufficient income or poor credit history.
rules.exemptions: Two-family owner-occupied dwellings, rooms in an owner- or resident-occupied single home (as it pertains to familial status per the guide)
rules.quoted_span: nationality, or source of lawful income.
rules.interaction: State anti-discrimination law; guide says nothing about criminal-history screening.

all.unavailable: two-family owner-occupied dwelling or room in an owner-occupied home

notes: Guide states NJ has no state law that establishes, governs or controls rents (municipal rent control only; Newly Constructed Multiple Dwellings Law N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.5 exempts new buildings from local control for 30 years): no state rent_increase_limits rule, a valid no_rule finding. Guide gives no effective dates. Application fees: only says landlord may request reasonable rental application fees, no cap or statute named: no rule. No criminal-history screening rule or algorithmic rent-setting content. Source-of-income record is lower confidence (single clause in discrimination summary).
